strokeOrder: draw the short upper stroke from left to right
lift, begin at the left and curve down, then run out to the right along the base, rising slightly at the end
lift, draw the left tick of the dakuten down to the right
lift, draw the right tick down to the right
strokeOrderNote: KanjiVG's 03054 file records ご as four stroke paths in this order and direction: こ's two strokes (the upper stroke and the lower curve), then the dakuten's two ticks, the left one first, each drawn down to the right; so there are three pen lifts.

strokeOrderSource.citation: KanjiVG, kanji/03054.svg, hiragana ご (U+3054 HIRAGANA LETTER GO), four stroke paths kvg:03054-s1 to s4 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0)
strokeOrderSource.variation: KanjiVG stores each stroke as one directed path in writing order: s1 to s2 are こ's strokes, the same paths as in its file for こ, kanji/03053.svg; s3 and s4 are the dakuten, the left tick first and then the right one, each drawn down to the right. Only the order and direction are taken from that file. The learner path's coordinates are the bundled Noto Sans JP outline's own medial line, so the print glyph's proportions, not KanjiVG's handwriting-style ones, decide where each stroke runs. KanjiVG's upper stroke of こ ends in a small turn down and back to the left that the print glyph does not show.
